title: The Bhakti and Sufi Movements: Faith as a Social Force

questions.question: The Divya Prabandham, called the 'Tamil Veda', is the collected hymn book of which saints?
questions.rationale: The Divya Prabandham gathers the Vaishnava hymns of the twelve Alvars, compiled by Nathamuni; the Nayanars were the parallel Shaiva saints of the Tevaram tradition.

questions.question: Shankara, who founded mathas at Sringeri, Puri, Dwarka, and Badrinath, taught the doctrine of:
questions.rationale: Shankara (c. 788-820) taught Advaita — the identity of soul and Brahman, with the world of appearances illusory; Ramanuja, Madhva, and Vallabha later countered with their own schools.

questions.question: Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita made the spiritual path rest chiefly on:
questions.rationale: Ramanuja (1017-1137) taught qualified non-dualism and made loving devotion with surrender to a personal God — served in temple worship — the road to liberation.

questions.question: Kabir's verses, attacking both mullah and pandit, are collected in which work?
questions.rationale: The Bijak is the scripture of the Kabirpanth, collecting the weaver-saint's nirguna verses; his hymns also appear in the Sikh Adi Granth.

questions.question: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at:
questions.rationale: Nanak was born at Talwandi, now Nankana Sahib in Pakistan; he built the Sikh discipline of naam japo, kirat karo, and vand chhako, with sangat and langar.

questions.question: Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, the most recited retelling of the Rama story, is written in:
questions.rationale: Tulsidas (1532-1623) composed the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi, the language of the eastern Hindi region; Surdas sang Krishna in Braj bhasha.

questions.question: The Varkari saints Namadeva and Tukaram undertook annual pilgrimage to which deity's shrine?
questions.rationale: The Maharashtra Varkari tradition walks each year to Pandharpur to the god Vitthala; Namadeva's abhangas entered the Adi Granth and Tukaram was the movement's last great singer.

questions.question: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti, whose dargah at Ajmer remains India's most visited shrine, died in:
questions.rationale: Muinuddin Chishti settled at Ajmer about 1191 and died there in 1236; his spiritual chain ran through Bakhtiar Kaki and Baba Farid to Nizamuddin Auliya (d. 1325).

questions.question: Bahauddin Zakariya, who accepted state service and opposed devotional music, led which Sufi order from Multan?
questions.rationale: Bahauddin Zakariya (d. 1262) headed the Suhrawardi order at Multan, accepting rulers' patronage as a tool of influence — in contrast to Chishti aloofness from courts.

questions.question: In Sufi practice, sama refers to:
options: The disciple's pledge to the pir
questions.rationale: Sama is the audition of devotional music, approved by Chishtis and associated with qawwali (perfected by Amir Khusrau); zikr is remembrance, bait the pledge, and urs the death anniversary.
